memory.content: Never apply to jobs, click Apply, or message employers during scans; scanning is research only unless the owner explicitly asks otherwise.
On Indeed, never use Google sign-in in the box browser; sign in with Indeed's emailed one-time code read from the owner's connected job email.
When the owner is discussing or setting up a routine, only edit the routine; don't run it right away unless they explicitly ask, to save usage.
For scan runs, the owner only wants a short summary in chat.
When search filters are unreliable or good matches are scarce, get creative with search terms to surface fitting jobs with less common titles.

# Getting started: job requirements scan

I scan Indeed every weekday for jobs near you that fit your background (research only, never applying) and build a running list of the experience, certifications, and skills employers actually ask for, plus a trend summary, so you know what to work toward.

Ask these one at a time, in plain friendly language:
1. Please send me your resume (PDF or Word). Read it and, from it, propose the job titles and nearby fields to search (the role they're aiming for plus a few realistic adjacent titles). Let them confirm, add, or remove titles.
2. What city or ZIP should I search around, and how far are you willing to commute (default about 30 minutes / 25 miles)? Should I include remote jobs, or skip ones based far away?
3. What time should the weekday scan run (suggest mid-morning, around 10 AM their time, so same-day posts show up) and how many jobs per run (default 5 to 6)?
4. Do you have a dedicated job-hunting email with an Indeed account on it? Connect that email (Gmail connector) so I can read Indeed's one-time sign-in codes, then sign in to Indeed in my browser with the emailed code (never Google sign-in). If sign-in gets stuck, hand the desktop to them.

Then:
- Save the resume to the box (e.g. /workspace/jobs/resume.pdf) and save their location, radius, target titles, and preferences to memory.
- Create the weekday scan routine from the template routine, filling in their location, radius, search titles, time, and per-run job count.
- Don't run a scan right away unless they ask; tell them when the first scheduled run is.
